_about: The outside services Almanac uses and what each costs. Prices are published list prices, checked on the date given; update them when a bill or a price page says otherwise. refresh.py adds the usage it can count.

services.role: Runs the game server, holds the database volume and the secrets.
services.setup: Personal organization, pay as you go. One shared-cpu-1x machine with 512 MB in Chicago (ord) that stops when idle; a 1 GB volume at /data; volume snapshots before each deploy.
services.pricing: Billed by the second while running. Monthly bills under $5 are waived for personal organizations.

services.role: Sign in with Google for accounts; the server checks each ID token.
services.setup: One OAuth client (web application) for almanac-game.fly.dev and localhost. The client ID is public; the client secret is never used by the app.

services.role: The offline question verifier, run from your machine. The game server never calls it.
services.setup: Your API key, used only in your terminal. Models: Haiku for bulk checks, Sonnet as the default, Opus once.
services.pricing: Per token and per web search; see the model rates under Financials.

services.role: Deliver phone and desktop notifications (Apple, Google and Mozilla run them for their browsers).
services.setup: A VAPID key pair stored as Fly secrets. Only the server's background sender talks to them.

services.role: Base images (node:22-slim, python:3.12-slim) and packages, fetched only when Fly builds a deploy.
Builds and deploys the project to the spec in CLAUDE.md.
services.setup: Runs on your machine against the OneDrive project folder.

costs.basis: shared-cpu-1x with 512 MB, $3.69 a month if it never stopped (Fly's listed price for Ashburn and Secaucus; Chicago may differ slightly). It stops when idle, so the real charge is a fraction of this.
$0.15 per GB-month of root file system, about 0.06 GB for this image.
1 GB at $0.15 per GB-month, charged whether or not the machine runs.
$0.08 per GB-month after the first 10 GB, which are free. The database is far under 10 GB.
$0.02 per GB in North America. A 100-player, 7-round game sends about 0.1 GB.
